title: A principal open defined by a nonzerodivisor is dense
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme] and let $a\in A$ be a non-zero-divisor. Then the principal open $D(a)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is topologically dense.

source.place: Tag 07ZU, affine-local calculation: the complement of a non-zero-divisor principal divisor is dense

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A_a)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ induced by localization has image the principal open $D(a)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. Thus $D(a)$ is the range of the contraction map on prime spectra.

source.place: Tag 00E4, the affine localization identifies Spec(A_a) with D(a)

proof.text: By [lem-pc-dense-range-comap-minimal-primes], this range is dense if every minimal prime ideal $I$ of $A$ is the contraction of a prime ideal of $A_a$.

For every minimal prime $I$ of $A$, [lem-pc-minimal-prime-avoids-nonzerodivisor] gives $a\notin I$, i.e. $I\in D(a)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (ii), $D(a)$ is the image of $\operatorname{Spec}(A_a)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, so $I=\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak P)$ for a prime $\mathfrak P$ of $A_a$. Therefore every minimal prime is in the range, and $D(a)$ is dense.
